newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: UBS joins forces with Pakistani brokerage.
newsitem.headline: UBS joins forces with Pakistani brokerage.

text.p: The Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) and Pakistan's Global Securities Ltd (GSL), a brokerage house, announced a joint venture on Friday.
Khawaja Iqbal Hassan, a GSL executive, told a news conference the new company would call itself UBS Securities and had sought the approval of the state Corporate Law Authority.
UBS Securities would be owned 51 percent by UBS and 49 percent by GSL. Hassan did not disclose the company's capital.

"After establishing a close working relationship, UBS and GSL signed a joint venture in November 1996 that incorporates cooperation in various areas including equity sales and research, corporate and project finance, investment advisory and dealing in debt securities," another GSL executive, Farhan Mehmood, said.
The announcement boosted sentiment at the Karachi Stock Exchange, where the 100-index rose 7.28 points, or 0.46 percent, to 1,594.38 on Friday amid 108 gainers and 98 losers.
GSL accounts for an estimated seven percent of the turnover on the Karachi bourse, Pakistan's biggest.
"Our objective is to actively participate in the development of Pakistan's capital markets and play a leading role in the country's economic growth," Mehmood said.
UBS East Asia Region chairman Lim Ho Kee said: "We will contribute in the development of the capital market. We are not here to make money, we are here to develop the market.
"The debt market is in an embronic stage. As the market grows, we will have a greater role," he said.
Kee, who is based in Singapore, said the new venture would try to raise the confidence of international investors.
"We have played a leading role in the development of Pakisan's capital markets ever since inception," said Mehmood.

"Since inception we have successfully completed transactions cumulatively worth 22 billion rupees ($630 million) and are currently mandated for transactions worth 15 billion rupees ($360 million)," he added.
GSL placed $98 million of orders for vouchers of Pakistan's telecom utility, now Pakistan Telecommunication Co Ltd (PTCL) PTCA.KA ), when the government floated them in September 1994.
In February 1997, GSL acted as financial advisers for the flotation of $150 million of bonds convertible into PTCL shares -- Pakistan's first long-term primary market deal in 17 months.
Karachi Stock Exchange president Arif Habib said UBS's experience would benefit Pakistan's capital market.
